newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen flat-off $0.50- trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen flat-off $0.50- trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, weighed down by hefty marketings and Thursday's large slaughter, packer buyers and dealers said.

Iowa/southern Minnesota sources said top prices for hogs delivered to the plant Friday were seen steady to $0.50 lower at $58.50 to $59.00. Some buyers said they had enough hogs for Friday operations and were buying for Monday already.
Illinois buyers said top hog prices at the plant could be steady to $0.50 lower, ranging from $57.00 to $57.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants were seen steady to $0.50 lower in a range of $57.00 to $57.50.
Eastern Corn Belt buyers said rain Wednesday and Thursday kept farmers from harvesting in parts of Indiana and Illinois.

The delay spurred an increase in marketings and revealed slight weight gains in hogs held back while farmers were in the fields, sources there said. Hogs were averaging one to two lbs heavier this seek, sources there said. Favorable weather this fall also contributed to the weight gains, dealers said.
Greater weights and hog numbers were expected to press pork prices Thursday and weaken cash hog prices Friday.
